Qualcomm Brings World's First 48-Core 10nm Chip For Servers
Big ol chip. Why cant we make stuff bigger?

Production waste, and heat, mostly. The bigger a chip is, the more likely it is that something goes wrong during production. Which leads to the chip being non functional, or only functional at lower speeds, with less cores, or less memory. Heat is also a problem. Every component of a chip uses electricity, which generates heat. The more components a chip has, the more heat it generates, and the more likely it becomes for those components to get into each others way when it comes to getting the heat out of the chip.
Very impressive! 10nm feature size...hard to imagine we can go any smaller than that.

The difference between this and Intel x86 cores is insane. And I mean in terms of speed, not energy consumption. A 6 core x86 will run circles around this, and 72 core chips are already available. The gap is wide enough Intel has been beating ARM in performance per watt, not just raw performance for at least 4 or 5 years now. The reason ARM still has the bulk of the mobile market is price. So there really isn't a point to an ARM "server" chip.
